title: The Last Harbor
premise: In 1893, on a storm-battered northern coast, Astrid Winterbourne keeps the lighthouse and the silences of a coastal town built on smuggled fortunes. When a mute child is abandoned at her door carrying a locket with Astrid's own face inside, she realizes the boy belongs to the Harrow family—the shipping dynasty whose wealth was laundered through her late husband's workshop. As the great storms of that winter destroy the harbor, Astrid must decide whether to burn the ledger proving the Harrows' crimes or use it to save the town. She chooses the town, exposing the family at the cost of the lighthouse itself, and leaves the harbor not in defeat but as the child's guardian, finally free of the silence she kept for fifteen years.
about_author: Yara Delacroix is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse keepers' logs along the North Atlantic coast. Her novels are known for their salt-weathered prose and their fascination with what ordinary people bury to survive.

chapters.title: The Door in the Dark
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. During the first storm of winter, Astrid finds an infant-swaddled boy of six left at the lighthouse door, clutching a locket bearing her own younger face. The note reads only: forget the face. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in tenderness, as fifteen years of careful invisibility begin to crack.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brings
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The boy, whom she names Finn, cannot or will not speak. Cleaning his clothes, Astrid finds a scrap of Harrow shipping paper. Flashbacks reveal her husband Edmund's death and the workshop where he built more than lamps. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing, suspicion taking root.

chapters.title: The Ledger Under the Floor
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Searching Edmund's ruined workshop before the next gale, she uncovers a hidden ledger recording payments from Augustus Harrow—proof the family used the workshop to move stolen cargo. Emotional beat: the sickening clarity that her marriage was entangled in crime she never chose.

chapters.title: A Visit from Ashore
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Astrid and Silas Harrow, Augustus's cold son. Silas arrives asking polite questions about a lost shipment and a missing woman—Finn's mother. His courtesy is a threat. Emotional beat: the mask of civility stretched over menace; Astrid lies well but not perfectly.

chapters.title: The Town That Forgot
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. In the village, Astrid probes old neighbors and learns how many families were paid to stay silent over the decades—including her own father-in-law. Finn begins speaking in fragments, repeating words he heard in the Harrow house. Emotional beat: complicity everywhere; loneliness deepening even among people.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Water
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. After the worst storm yet, a drowned woman washes ashore wearing a matching locket—Finn's mother. Among her effects: a letter naming Augustus and begging Astrid by name for help. Emotional beat: horror transmuting into resolve; the silence has killed someone.

chapters.title: Silas's Bargain
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Silas and Astrid. Silas offers Astrid money and passage away if she surrenders the child and any papers. He reveals he knows about the ledger—and that the storms have given the family cover to burn the workshop themselves. Emotional beat: temptation and fury; Astrid understands time is nearly gone.

chapters.title: Fire on the Headland
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The workshop burns in the night—arson meant to erase everything. Astrid races through the storm to salvage the ledger, saving it barely, while Finn, watching the flames, finally speaks his mother's last words aloud. Climactic emotional beat: loss crystallizing into open war.

chapters.title: The Great Storm
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Astrid and Silas. During the season's final, catastrophic storm, Astrid uses the ledger to rally the indebted townsfolk, then confronts Silas at the harbor as his ship founders. She saves him from drowning—an act that breaks the cycle of power's cruelty. Emotional beat: climax; mercy as the sharpest weapon.

chapters.title: Leaving the Light
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. With the Harrows exposed and the lighthouse decommissioned after storm damage, Astrid testifies, buries Finn's mother properly, and departs the harbor with the boy. The final image: two lockets joined on one chain. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—inheritance refused, memory carried forward instead of buried.
